competitive_landscape: Premium transfer here is mature: helicopters (Monacair), charter tenders and an existing electric harbour shuttle all serve a market that pays top price for speed and arrival. The gap is a fast, silent, sea-level coastal tier that beats road gridlock without helicopter cost or noise — squarely aligned with Monaco's flagship environmental positioning.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The entire core Riviera shuttle market — Monaco↔Nice (~9 nm), ↔Cap-Ferrat, ↔Cannes (~22 nm), ↔San Remo (~12 nm) — sits well inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope over protected Ligurian-Sea waters, with willing-to-pay-anything demand and a host nation that prizes the zero-emission story.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Opens the longer marquee coastal runs — Monaco↔St-Tropez (~50 nm), ↔Portofino (~95 nm), ↔Corsica — as premium experiential cruises beyond the all-electric range, with no charging dependency on smaller Riviera ports.

regulatory_note: Monaco maintains its own maritime authority (Direction des Affaires Maritimes) and harbour administration; cross-border Riviera legs touch French and Italian waters. Monaco's stated decarbonisation agenda (Prince Albert II Foundation; commitment to carbon neutrality) makes a zero-emission foiling service politically and reputationally favoured.
seasonality: Demand peaks hard around the May Grand Prix and September Yacht Show, with a strong summer Riviera season May-September; the resident UHNW base keeps premium transfer demand alive year-round. Winter Ligurian swell is the main weather constraint, which foiling smooths.

summary: Monaco is a 2 km² sovereign principality with the densest concentration of ultra-high-net-worth residents and superyachts on earth, two working harbours (Port Hercule and Port de Fontvieille), and a calendar of globally televised events — the Formula 1 Grand Prix (May) and the Monaco Yacht Show (September) chief among them — that turn the coast into a wall of demand. It already runs the world's only scheduled solar-electric harbour shuttle (the Bateau Bus) and, under the Prince Albert II Foundation, has made decarbonisation a point of national pride. The Riviera coast it anchors — Nice, Cap-Ferrat, Cannes, San Remo, St-Tropez — is a string of short, protected, pay-any-price hops today served by helicopter, road and diesel tenders. A fast, silent, all-electric foiling shuttle tier is almost purpose-built for this market.
tagline: The highest concentration of yachts, wealth and marquee events on the Mediterranean — and a sovereign that has staked its identity on going green. The premium electric water-shuttle belongs here.
